analysis.overall: You spent 86% of the day in range with a flat overnight baseline, though heavy meals in the evening and mid-morning caused temporary spikes over 200 mg/dL that needed repeated corrections.

events.title: Afternoon dip and flat coast
events.description: An early afternoon drop touched 70 mg/dL, but a 50g lunch balanced it out, keeping glucose steady in the high 70s for hours.

events.title: Evening dinner spike
events.description: A 40g meal shot glucose up to a peak of 207 mg/dL, requiring several small correction doses over two hours to pull it back into range.

events.title: Smooth overnight baseline
events.description: After late-night correction activity settled, glucose stayed nicely parked in the 80–110 mg/dL range until dawn.

events.title: Mid-morning rise and steep drop
events.description: Multiple carb entries in quick succession pushed levels up to 220 mg/dL, prompting repeated correction boluses that are now dropping glucose sharply around noon.

analysis.watch_for_tomorrow: Watch out for stacking multiple small correction doses during high peaks, as the cumulative insulin can cause a rapid drop later on.
